headline: Initial sales commitments for 5-year data migration and HL7 integration were not reflected in the SOW, causing client escalation and project delays.

actors.name: Jake Morris
actors.summary: Initiated the sales process with broad promises, failed to ensure SOW aligned with client expectations, and downplayed internal concerns about scope.

actors.name: Rebecca Chen
actors.summary: The primary client contact who confirmed critical requirements and escalated when the delivered scope did not match initial promises.

actors.name: Olivia Grant
actors.summary: Identified and flagged a mismatch between Jake's initial promises and the standard contract scope early in the process.

actors.name: Ana Silva
actors.summary: Led the implementation, identified the scope discrepancy with the client, sought internal clarification, and managed the adjusted project.

actors.name: Marcus Webb
actors.summary: The client's IT lead who questioned the implementation scope during the project based on original expectations.

actors.name: Lisa Park
actors.summary: Intervened in the escalation, took ownership of the discrepancy, and provided a resolution plan to the client.

events.title: Proposed 5-year history and HL7 support
events.detail: Jake Morris proposed that Brightdesk would migrate Acme Health's full 5-year patient-engagement history and support HL7 feeds out of the box during the demo follow-up. This set the client's initial expectations for the project scope.

events.title: Confirmed critical need for 5-year history
events.detail: Rebecca Chen confirmed that the full 5-year history was critical for Acme Health's compliance reporting, reinforcing her understanding of the scope as promised by Jake.

events.title: Acme Health SOW release
events.detail: Jake Morris announced that the Acme Health Statement of Work (SOW) was being sent out, indicating the deal was progressing.

events.title: Flagged scope discrepancy
events.detail: Olivia Grant identified that the 'standard implementation package' only covered 24 months of history via CSV and no HL7, conflicting with Jake's earlier promises.

events.title: Dismissed scope concerns
events.detail: Jake Morris dismissed Olivia Grant's concerns about the scope discrepancy, stating 'they're fine' and details could be sorted out in implementation, thereby allowing the misaligned SOW to proceed.

events.title: SOW signed with standard scope
events.detail: The SOW was signed, formalizing the scope as a standard implementation, 24-month history migration via CSV, and a go-live target of September 30.

events.title: Kickoff and data request
events.detail: Ana Silva conducted the project kickoff with Rebecca Chen and Marcus Webb, and requested the data extract from LegacyCRM.

events.title: Set test import milestone
events.detail: Ana Silva set the next milestone as a test import by August 29, communicating a clear deliverable for the client.

events.title: Completed 24-month test import
events.detail: Ana Silva successfully completed the test import of the 24-month dataset, reporting 1.2M records matched and project on track for go-live.

events.title: Client questioned scope discrepancy
events.detail: Marcus Webb questioned why only 24 months of data were imported when they sent the full 5-year extract, and inquired about the HL7 feed, highlighting the client's expectations not aligning with the implemented scope.

events.title: Internal clarification on scope
events.detail: Ana Silva raised the client's scope concerns internally to Jake Morris, asking if additional promises regarding 5-year history and HL7 were made.

events.title: Admitted mentioning full history
events.detail: Jake Morris admitted he 'might have mentioned the full history' in the demo, suggesting to proceed with it despite the SOW, without fully understanding the implications.

events.title: Explained scope change impact
events.detail: Ana Silva clarified that changing to a 5-year history (4x volume, different schema) and HL7 integration were significant scope changes requiring 3-4 extra weeks, demonstrating the complexity Jake underestimated.

events.title: Promised update on scope by Friday
events.detail: Ana Silva promised Marcus Webb that she would check with her team regarding the 5-year history and HL7, and provide an answer by Friday (Sept 5).

events.title: Missed scope clarification deadline
events.detail: Ana Silva documented that the scope question was still open with sales, blocking progress and putting the go-live at risk, indicating the promised answer by Sept 5 was not delivered.

events.title: Client escalated directly to sales
events.detail: Rebecca Chen escalated to Jake Morris, citing his initial promise, the missed deadline for an answer (Sept 5), and the impending go-live, demanding an explanation.

events.title: VP Customer Success intervened
events.detail: Lisa Park intervened in the escalation, requesting the full history of promises versus SOW details from Jake and Ana to understand the situation.

events.title: Reiterated prior warning
events.detail: Olivia Grant reiterated her earlier warning from July 21, confirming she had previously flagged the discrepancy between promised scope and standard SOW.

events.title: Committed to full scope and new timeline
events.detail: Lisa Park acknowledged the discrepancy, committed to migrating the full 5-year history at no extra cost, moved the go-live to October 21, and promised an HL7 phase 2 plan by September 26, resolving the immediate client concern.

events.title: Updated ticket with approved scope changes
events.detail: Ana Silva updated the implementation ticket with the scope changes approved by Lisa Park, including the 5-year history, revised go-live date, and HL7 plan deadline.

events.title: Delivered HL7 plan and passed 5-year test
events.detail: Ana Silva sent the HL7 phase 2 plan to the client and confirmed that the 5-year migration test import (4.6M records) had passed, fulfilling the new commitments.

commitments.what: Migrate full 5-year patient-engagement history from LegacyCRM
commitments.statusReason: Initially broken by the signed SOW [T1], but re-committed by Lisa Park [E7] and successfully tested/implemented by Ana Silva [T5].

commitments.what: HL7 feeds supported out of the box
commitments.statusReason: This commitment was not included in the signed SOW [T1] and required a separate integration project, as clarified by Ana Silva [C6]. It was later re-scoped as a Phase 2 project [E7, T5].

commitments.what: Details regarding scope can be sorted out during implementation
commitments.statusReason: This claim was proven false when the client raised significant issues during implementation due to the scope discrepancy, leading to an escalation [E4, E6].
The go-live was put at risk due to unresolved scope questions [T3] and later explicitly moved to October 21 as part of the resolution [E7].
Ana Silva reported completion of the test import on August 29 [E3].

commitments.what: Provide an answer on 5-year history and HL7 by Friday
commitments.statusReason: Rebecca Chen explicitly stated that no answer was received by September 5, leading to her escalation [E6].

commitments.what: Migrate the full 5-year history at no extra cost
commitments.statusReason: Ana Silva confirmed the 5-year migration test import passed successfully on September 26 [T5].
The commitment was made and implementation progressed towards this date, but the record does not extend to confirm the actual go-live on Oct 21 [E7, T4, T5].

commitments.what: Scope HL7 as a Phase 2 with a firm plan by September 26
commitments.statusReason: Ana Silva sent the HL7 phase 2 plan to Rebecca and Marcus on September 26 [T5].

phases.name: Proposal & SOW
phases.summary: Sales proposed a 5-year history migration and HL7 support. Deal Desk identified a scope mismatch with the standard package, but sales proceeded with a standard SOW, which was signed.

phases.name: Implementation Discrepancy
phases.summary: Implementation began, and a 24-month test import was completed. The client then questioned the 24-month scope and HL7, leading to internal clarification where sales acknowledged the initial over-commitment.

phases.name: Internal Block & Escalation
phases.summary: Implementation was blocked awaiting scope clarification from sales. A promised client update was missed, leading to the client escalating to sales and subsequently to the VP of Customer Success.

phases.name: Resolution & Re-commitment
phases.summary: The VP of Customer Success committed to the full 5-year migration at no extra cost, rescheduled go-live, and provided a plan for HL7 Phase 2. The 5-year migration test passed.

whatWentWrong.title: Unverified Sales Commitments
whatWentWrong.detail: Sales committed to specific features (5-year history, HL7) without confirming they were part of the standard package or accounted for in the SOW [E1]. This created a mismatch between client expectations and the contracted scope from the outset.

whatWentWrong.title: Failure to Act on Early Warning Signs
whatWentWrong.detail: A Deal Desk agent explicitly flagged the scope discrepancy (24 months, no HL7) before the SOW was signed [C2]. This warning was dismissed by sales, leading to a signed contract that did not align with client needs [C3, T1].

whatWentWrong.title: Lack of Clear Handover from Sales to Implementation
whatWentWrong.detail: The detailed scope promised by sales was not effectively transferred or clarified to the implementation team, who discovered the discrepancy only when the client raised it [E4, C4]. This indicates a process gap in ensuring alignment post-sale.

whatWentWrong.title: Delayed Internal Resolution Process
whatWentWrong.detail: After the client's initial query and an internal promise to update them by a specific date [E5], the internal team failed to provide a resolution or update, leaving the client in the dark for over a week [T3, E6]. This delay directly triggered the client's escalation.

contradictions.title: Sales Promise vs. Signed SOW Scope
contradictions.detail: Jake Morris's initial email to Acme Health explicitly promised 'full patient-engagement history (all 5 years)' and 'HL7 feeds are supported out of the box' [E1]. However, the signed SOW only covered '24-month history migration from LegacyCRM via CSV' with no mention of HL7 [T1, C2].

contradictions.title: Dismissed Concerns vs. Critical Client Issue
contradictions.detail: When the scope discrepancy was raised internally, Jake Morris stated, 'they're fine, we can sort out the details in implementation' [C3]. In reality, this scope difference became a critical issue for the client during implementation, leading to an escalation and project delays [E4, E6, T3].

contradictions.title: Promised Update vs. Client Communication
contradictions.detail: Ana Silva promised Marcus Webb an update on the 5-year history and HL7 scope by 'Friday' (September 5) [E5]. However, on September 15, Rebecca Chen escalated, explicitly stating, 'We were also promised an answer by Sept 5 and haven't heard anything' [E6].

openQuestions: What specific internal process changes will be implemented to ensure sales commitments are accurately reflected in SOWs and communicated to implementation teams?
Was there any attempt by Jake Morris or his manager to resolve the scope issue internally or communicate with the client between Ana's internal flag on Sept 1 and Rebecca's escalation on Sept 15?
What were the reasons for the delay in providing the promised update to the client by September 5?
What was the ultimate outcome of the go-live on October 21 and the client's satisfaction with the HL7 Phase 2 plan?
Is there an internal process for sales to get Deal Desk/Implementation approval for custom requirements (like 5-year history or HL7) before they are proposed to the client?
clientReply: Rebecca, I sincerely apologize for the significant miscommunication and the issues this has caused. You are absolutely right that our initial communications, specifically Jake's email of July 14, set clear expectations for a full 5-year history migration and HL7 support. The signed SOW did not reflect these critical requirements, which was our error. To resolve this, we are committing to migrate your full 5-year history at no additional cost. Your new go-live date will be October 21 to accommodate this. We have also provided the plan for HL7 integration as a Phase 2, with work starting November 2. We are implementing stricter internal processes to ensure commitments made during sales are accurately captured and delivered throughout implementation, preventing such discrepancies in the future. I am personally overseeing your account to ensure a successful resolution.
